inspection_summary: Inspected all 1,217 normalized lines, including the introduction, all six mathematical regime/method sections, the complete large-values proof, references, and back matter. The text layer is coherent despite formula-layout risk. The source progresses from easy Dirichlet-series moment evaluation through strip error terms and unconditional lower bounds to critical-line explicit formulas, spectral error control, and an RH-conditional short-interval upper bound derived from large-value tails.

sections_inspected.label: Front matter and introduction
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Defines the short-interval moment object, records the functional equation, and decomposes analysis into sigma regimes.

sections_inspected.label: Section 2: sigma > 1
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Uses absolute Dirichlet-series convergence and diagonal/off-diagonal separation to obtain a linear-in-H asymptotic.

sections_inspected.label: Section 3: sigma = 1
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Packages boundary-line mean values into error terms and extends the asymptotic to complex moment parameters via contour methods.

sections_inspected.label: Section 4: critical strip
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Surveys mean-square, fourth-moment, and general higher-moment asymptotics, comparing divisor-problem and moment-abscissa controls.

sections_inspected.label: Section 5: unconditional lower bound
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Transfers a nonvanishing estimate from absolute convergence to the strip through an optimal double-exponential kernel and parameter balancing.

sections_inspected.label: Section 6: critical-line mean values
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Relates second- and fourth-moment error terms to oscillatory and spectral representations, short-interval thresholds, and higher-moment obstructions.

sections_inspected.label: Section 7: critical-line short intervals
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Gives unconditional lower bounds and an RH-conditional upper bound, then proves the latter through large-value tails and prime Dirichlet-polynomial moments.

sections_inspected.label: References and publication back matter
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Bibliographic provenance and author/publication metadata; no additional mathematical argument.

accepted_units.title: Short-interval moments split into four sigma regimes
accepted_units.why_material: The paper defines its common moment functional and explains why integer moments and the functional equation reduce the study to four qualitatively different regions, with the critical line singled out as the hard case.
accepted_units.context_note: Self-contained setup for all later units; the abstract at lines 11-18 supplies only a shorter preview.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The displayed functional equation and moment definition matter, but the regime decomposition is recoverable from the checked prose and text-layer formulas.

accepted_units.title: Absolute convergence turns moments into a diagonal main term
accepted_units.why_material: Expanding zeta^k as a divisor-coefficient Dirichlet series separates equal indices from oscillatory unequal indices; absolute convergence makes the latter bounded and yields a short-interval main term proportional to H.
accepted_units.context_note: Immutable v1 span; it is coherent without a v2 context repair.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The diagonal/off-diagonal mechanism is clear in prose; exact coefficients and the logarithmic denominator use displayed formulas.

accepted_units.title: At sigma=1, global error control yields short-interval asymptotics
accepted_units.why_material: The source isolates the pole-adjacent mean-square error, connects its pointwise bound to zeta on the 1-line, and records complex-k, logarithmic-derivative, and log-zeta mean values that imply a linear short-interval asymptotic.
accepted_units.context_note: The Hooley-Huxley contour is identified as the non-elementary ingredient; the span ends with the short-interval consequence.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Several constants and powers are display-dependent, but the error-term-to-local-asymptotic logic is explicit in prose.

accepted_units.title: Secondary terms and error scales inside the critical strip
accepted_units.why_material: The mean square and fourth moment develop additional main terms away from sigma=1, and comparison of the spectral fourth-moment error with those terms identifies where the nominal expansion ceases to be informative.
accepted_units.context_note: Immutable v1 span; it includes the local comparison needed to interpret the displayed fourth-moment expansion.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Exact exponents and zeta-factor constants depend on the displayed formulas; the hierarchy of terms is recoverable from the surrounding prose.

accepted_units.unit_type: general-moment control by a critical abscissa
accepted_units.title: Higher-moment remainders are parameterized by sigma-star
accepted_units.why_material: After special low moments stop generalizing, the source expresses a general 2k-th moment remainder in terms of the least line on which a T^(1+epsilon) moment bound is available and shows how this produces explicit but nonuniform exponents.
accepted_units.context_note: The span contrasts the reusable sigma-star mechanism with cumbersome k-specific exponent lists and records its deterioration near sigma=1.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Displayed exponents are essential for quantitative reuse; prose fully identifies the abstraction and its limitation.

accepted_units.title: Two controls dominate in complementary parts of the strip
accepted_units.why_material: The source compares a divisor-problem mean-square parameter with the moment-abscissa parameter, explaining that one controls remainders near sigma=1 while the other is better near its threshold, then instantiates the comparison for several moments.
accepted_units.context_note: Immutable v1 span; it requires the definition immediately before it and the continuation immediately after it for safe standalone interpretation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The complementary-regime claim is explicit in prose; exact remainder exponents are formula-dependent.

accepted_units.title: Ramachandra's kernel transports a lower bound across sigma
accepted_units.why_material: A lower bound in the absolutely convergent region is carried to the critical strip by a residue representation with double-exponential horizontal decay, followed by two parameter choices that first prevent the target integral from being tiny and then close the bound.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the theorem, full proof mechanism, and the source's argument that this kernel method cannot push H substantially below a multiple of log log T.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Contour geometry, kernel decay, and balancing inequalities use displays, but all transitions and the method barrier are recoverable from checked prose.

accepted_units.title: Atkinson represents the mean-square error by dual oscillatory sums
accepted_units.why_material: The critical-line mean-square error is converted into two explicit oscillatory sums with complementary ranges, making the error term accessible to cancellation estimates rather than only integral identities.
accepted_units.context_note: The span defines E(T), states the explicit formula, and gives the phase and weight behavior needed to understand the representation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Highly display-dependent; the normalized formulas are usable for mechanism-level segmentation, while exact phase typography should be checked before equation-level reuse.

accepted_units.title: Riemann-Siegel sums and error increments control local zeta size
accepted_units.why_material: A structurally different Riemann-Siegel-based formula estimates the same error term, and a local averaging inequality turns increments of E into pointwise control of zeta, exposing how global error exponents set short-interval asymptotic thresholds.
accepted_units.context_note: Also records opposing omega behavior and the conjectured T^(1/4+epsilon) scale, which delimit what error-term improvement would mean.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The double sums and omega factors require the displays; the representation comparison and localization bridge are clear in prose.

accepted_units.unit_type: spectral representation of a smoothed fourth moment
accepted_units.title: Gaussian smoothing opens a spectral route to the fourth-moment error
accepted_units.why_material: Motohashi's Gaussian-smoothed fourth moment is expressed through spectral data via trace formulas; resulting upper, omega, and mean-square bounds for E2 translate into a concrete short-interval length at which a fourth-moment asymptotic is unconditional.
accepted_units.context_note: The span joins the representation, why smoothing is necessary, the spectral quantities, and the downstream H threshold.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Exact spectral coefficients and smoothing ranges are display-dependent; the transform, convergence role, and threshold are textually recoverable.

accepted_units.title: Critical-line higher moments expose both equivalences and bottlenecks
accepted_units.why_material: The survey contrasts the lone strong twelfth-moment bound with absent asymptotics for k>=3, identifies all-moment T^(1+epsilon) bounds as equivalent to Lindelof, and links the sixth moment to a ternary additive divisor conjecture.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a compact obstruction map rather than a proof.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The logical claims are prose-supported; the exact moment exponents appear in readable displays.

accepted_units.title: Critical-line moments have the conjectured logarithmic lower scale
accepted_units.why_material: Theorem 2 strengthens the general lower bound on the critical line to H times a k-squared logarithmic power and records the arithmetic Euler-product constant and the log-log interval threshold.
accepted_units.context_note: The proof is cited rather than reproduced, so the unit supports the result and scale but not its internal derivation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The exponent and Euler product are display-dependent; the range and interpretation are explicit in prose.

accepted_units.title: Large values replace pointwise RH bounds in moment control
accepted_units.why_material: The source explains why known unconditional upper bounds are sparse, distinguishes RH from Lindelof, and contrasts a weak pointwise RH consequence with Soundararajan's essentially sharp full-interval moment bound based on the distribution of log|zeta|.
accepted_units.context_note: Sets the strategic motivation for the short-interval adaptation that follows.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The quantitative logarithmic exponents use displays; the method comparison is prose-supported.

accepted_units.title: The full-interval large-values method localizes to H=T^theta
accepted_units.why_material: Theorem 3 gives an RH-conditional upper bound matching the lower-bound logarithmic scale up to a vanishing exponent loss, while explicitly recording the fixed-power interval restriction and known exceptional low-moment ranges.
accepted_units.context_note: The source itself flags the unresolved extension to log-log-length intervals and removal of the exponent loss.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The exact O(1/log_3 T) exponent is display-dependent; the range, comparison, and limitations are clear.

accepted_units.title: Log|zeta| tails have Gaussian and V log V regimes
accepted_units.why_material: Theorem 4 partitions the admissible large-value range into two near-Gaussian decay regimes and a far-tail V log V regime, with explicit theta-dependent losses suited to a short interval.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the target estimate later converted into the moment bound.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Range endpoints and loss factors are equation-dependent but legible; the three-regime structure is explicit.

accepted_units.title: Discretized tails reduce the moment bound to a quadratic maximum
accepted_units.why_material: Small and very large values are disposed of directly, the middle range is discretized, and multiplying its measure by exp(2kU) reduces the problem to maximizing a concave quadratic, recovering the k-squared logarithmic exponent.
accepted_units.context_note: This span is the conceptual bridge from Theorem 4 to Theorem 3.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The discretization and maximization depend on displayed inequalities, all supported by explanatory prose.

accepted_units.title: RH turns large log|zeta| into a large prime polynomial
accepted_units.why_material: Three lemmas upper-bound log|zeta| by a smoothed Dirichlet polynomial, show prime powers contribute only a small error, and control high moments of prime polynomials on a short interval under the length-budget condition x^r<=H.
accepted_units.context_note: These are the reusable analytic inputs for the subsequent probability-style tail argument.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Coefficient weights and the moment inequality are display-dependent; their roles and hypotheses are recoverable.

accepted_units.title: Prime-range splitting converts moment estimates into tail decay
accepted_units.why_material: The proof chooses a V-dependent polynomial length, splits primes at a secondary cutoff, forces one piece to be large, and applies high moments with optimized integer orders to obtain Gaussian or V log V decay.
accepted_units.context_note: Immutable v1 span; it begins inside the lemma packet and stops before the second-prime-range estimate and final recombination, so a v2 repair is required.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula layout is dense, but the parameter choices, split, moment method, and resulting regimes are recoverable from the checked text.

accepted_units.title: The second prime range is bounded and the three tail regimes close
accepted_units.why_material: A parallel high-moment bound controls the longer-prime piece, case-specific choices verify the short-interval length constraint, and comparison with the first-piece bounds yields each of Theorem 4's three stated estimates.
accepted_units.context_note: Overlaps the end of the carried v1 unit to preserve the transition into the omitted completion.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Exact constants and iterated-log comparisons are display-dependent; the optimization and recombination are explicit in prose.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Error-term exponents as short-interval resolution limits
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: For the second and fourth moments, subtracting global asymptotics makes the error-term scale the effective minimum H at which a local main term is visible.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This comparison is established here only for the two low moments with explicit global formulas; it does not furnish higher-moment asymptotics.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Two-sided critical-line moment scale
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: On fixed-power short intervals, the unconditional lower bound and RH-conditional upper bound identify H times a k-squared logarithmic power as the common scale up to the stated vanishing loss.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The upper bound assumes RH and H=T^theta with fixed theta, while the lower bound covers integer k and much shorter intervals.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Modular route from RH to short-interval moments
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: RH supplies a prime-polynomial majorant; high-moment estimates yield piecewise tail decay; discretizing and optimizing those tails yields the moment exponent.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The chain is solver- and parameter-specific analytic evidence, depends on fixed theta, and retains an O(1/log_3 T) exponent loss.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Complementary representations of critical-line errors
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Oscillatory sums, Riemann-Siegel correlations, and smoothed spectral sums are alternative representations chosen to expose cancellation or convergence unavailable in the raw moment integral.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: They concern different error terms and cannot be interchanged without their distinct weights, ranges, and spectral hypotheses.
